footnote: Source: State Council drone regulations, CCAR-92, CAAC consultation notice (2026-04-15), Xinhua (2025-12-10)
notes: The regulatory path. To run commercial deliveries with small drones, there are five steps before the first flight. One, registration: two mandatory national standards on real-name registration and remote identification took effect on May 1, 2026. Two, anyone flying a small drone needs a pilot license. Three, commercial flights must carry liability insurance. Four, specific-category operations need a risk assessment. China uses the SORA method, and in April 2026 CAAC put out a draft guide based on SORA 2.5 for comment. It has not taken effect yet. Five, the operating certificate itself, valid for 24 months under CCAR-92 and then renewed. The gate is real: flying without an operating certificate carries a fine of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. And staying below 120 meters does not mean free airspace: the areas around airports and key facilities are controlled. Because the assessment rules are changing, we prepare to the 2.5 draft and re-check when the final version is published. For us this is a barrier and a moat at once, and our first milestone is getting the certificate.
